standard_prerequisites.name: The functor of flat quotients of a quasi-coherent module, and its compatibility with an affine open covering
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, the functor $F_{flat}$ discussed in the surrounding section of the chapter (used at proof lines 6575-6577)
standard_prerequisites.use: Over the covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ the functor is the product of the functors of the pairs $(U_i, \mathcal{F}|_{U_i})$, which reduces the claim to the affine case, one closed condition at a time.

standard_prerequisites.name: The affine case of the universal flattening over an Artinian base
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: More on Algebra, label more-algebra-lemma-flattening-artinian-universal-property (invoked at proof line 6582)
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the universal flattening in the affine case, realized by a closed subscheme of the Artinian base, which is therefore also a flattening stratification.

core_obligations: Cover $X$ by affine opens $U_i$ and use that $F_{flat}$ is the product of the functors attached to the pairs $(U_i, \mathcal{F}|_{U_i})$, reducing to a single affine piece (proof lines 6575-6579).
Apply the affine statement over an Artinian base to the pair $(U_i, \mathcal{F}|_{U_i})$ (proof lines 6580-6582).
Conclude that the universal flattening exists and is given by a closed immersion of the base, so that it is a flattening stratification as well (statement lines 6569-6571).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to an affine piece by the product decomposition of the functor (proof lines 6575-6579).
The affine case over an Artinian base (proof lines 6580-6582).
Closed immersion and the stratification property (statement lines 6569-6571).
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces the universal flattening for an arbitrary quasi-coherent module on a scheme over the spectrum of an Artinian ring, and notes that it is cut out by a closed immersion of the base, so it is also a flattening stratification (statement lines 6565-6572). The proof reduces to the affine case by the product decomposition of the functor of flat quotients over an affine open covering, and then quotes the affine result over an Artinian base. The reduction and its packaging as a closed condition are the substance, so the claim is H2.
